report.summary: Chunk 1 of projection_worker.py: module docstring with guarantees, journal reading functions, and read-only view setup.
risks: complete_prefix_end | medium | Tail chunk logic may miss newline at very start of file; edge case where file has only one line without newline leads to infinite loop? | Test with single-line file without trailing newline.

scan_journal | low | line_number starts at 0 and increments per line; but first line after start offset gets line_number 1; for non-zero start, line numbering may be misleading. | Add test with non-zero start offset.

journal_position | low | If file shrinks between existence check and stat, hasher will be None and position resets to 0; this is acceptable fallback but may mask race conditions. | Document or add retry logic.

claims.text: The journal (``memory/events.local.jsonl``) is authoritative.  The vector index is derived.
claims.why: No code in this chunk asserts or uses this relationship; it is a design statement.

claims.text: Nothing in the operational append path is allowed to block on an embedding call, so this worker is the *only* component that is supposed to move the index forward -- and, because it is, it is also the component that owns :meth:`EventVectorStore.record_journal_watermark`.
claims.why: No code in this chunk references record_journal_watermark or the append path.

claims.text: Before it existed, every search reported ``freshness == "unanchored"``: freshness unknown.
claims.why: No code in this chunk references freshness or search reports.

claims.text: Progress is a byte offset into the journal, stored as a :class:`JournalPosition` watermark inside the index itself.
claims.why: journal_position returns a JournalPosition with byte offset; _prefix_hasher and complete_prefix_end operate on byte offsets.

claims.text: A run starts at the recorded watermark, never at zero, so restarting is cheap.
claims.why: Chunk does not contain the main run loop; no code reads a watermark from the index.

claims.text: the index is content-addressed (``UNIQUE(index_id, source_hash)`` with ``INSERT OR IGNORE``), so a replayed entry *cannot* duplicate
claims.why: No SQL schema or INSERT statements in this chunk.

claims.text: this worker filters entries whose ``source_hash`` is already in the index *before* embedding them, so a replay also costs nothing.
claims.why: No filtering logic present in this chunk.

claims.text: A watermark is recorded only after the projections for every journal byte below it are committed.
claims.why: No watermark recording code in this chunk.

claims.text: a killed run leaves a watermark that under-reports what landed, and the next run re-reads those entries, finds them already projected, embeds nothing, and moves the watermark up.
claims.why: No run logic or watermark update code in this chunk.

claims.text: the reverse -- a watermark ahead of the vectors -- is never written, because that would silently drop journal entries forever.
claims.why: No watermark recording logic in this chunk.

claims.text: ``content_hash`` on the watermark is the SHA-256 of the journal prefix ``[0, position)``.  On every run that prefix is re-hashed.
claims.why: journal_position computes SHA-256 of [0, end) via _prefix_hasher; _prefix_hasher streams the prefix and returns a hasher.

claims.text: A journal that was rewritten, truncated, or replaced fails the check and the run refuses with ``journal_forked`` instead of projecting a history that no longer matches the index.
claims.why: No 'journal_forked' error or refusal logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Only complete lines are consumed.  A trailing line with no ``\n`` is a writer mid-append, not a record.
claims.why: complete_prefix_end returns offset just past last newline; scan_journal breaks on lines not ending with b'\n'.

claims.text: The watermark stops before it.  Consuming it would parse a fragment and then skip the real record forever.
claims.why: No watermark update logic in this chunk.

claims.text: ``embedder_unavailable`` is an outage: the run stops, keeps the watermark it earned, and exits non-zero so a retry is obviously the right move.
claims.why: No embedder_unavailable handling in this chunk.

claims.text: ``model_drift`` is a correctness fault that survives a retry: :mod:`daedalus.memory.embeddings` refuses *before* writing, and this worker neither catches that refusal nor advances past it.
claims.why: No model_drift handling in this chunk.

claims.text: The worker resolves its :class:`EmbeddingSpec` **without calling the backend**: either by adopting the one index already recorded for this (provider, model, revision, normalization, projector) identity, or from the declared ``dimension`` (default :data:`DEFAULT_DIMENSION`).
claims.why: No spec resolution code in this chunk.

claims.text: ``model_revision`` defaults to ``None`` on purpose.
claims.why: No model_revision declaration in this chunk; it is mentioned in imports but not used.

claims.text: The shipped reader, ``daedalus.context_plan.latent_memory_seed_scores``, searches with no spec, so the spec it resolves has ``model_revision=None``.
claims.why: No reference to that reader in this chunk.

claims.text: Pinning a revision here produces a *different* ``index_id``, and ``daedalus context --latent`` would report ``index_unavailable`` against a perfectly good index.
claims.why: No index_id or context logic in this chunk.

claims.text: The worker warns when a revision is pinned.
claims.why: No warning code in this chunk.

claims.text: Drift is still caught, empirically, by the identity anchor in :mod:`daedalus.memory.embeddings` -- which is the control that works regardless of what the declaration claims.
claims.why: No drift detection code in this chunk.

claims.text: The pending backlog is held in memory.  One run reads every unprojected complete line before batching.  ``--limit`` is the bound for a journal that has grown far beyond what one run should chew through; there is no streaming path.
claims.why: scan_journal returns a list of JournalEntry objects; it has a limit parameter.

claims.text: Position is a byte offset, and only compares to byte offsets.
claims.why: journal_position returns byte offset; complete_prefix_end returns byte offset; scan_journal uses byte offsets.

claims.text: A caller that measures the same journal in line counts and passes that as a :class:`JournalPosition` will get a meaningless freshness answer.  Use :func:`journal_position` on both sides.
claims.why: No freshness comparison code in this chunk.

claims.text: A malformed or blank line is stepped over, not retried.  Both are counted and named in the report, and the watermark advances past them, because the journal is append-only and a broken line will never become valid.
claims.why: No watermark advancement or reporting code in this chunk.

claims.text: A silent ``skipped_malformed`` in a monitored run is a real finding, not noise.
claims.why: No skipped_malformed counter or reporting in this chunk.

claims.text: Nothing here schedules anything.
claims.why: No scheduling logic present in this chunk.

claims.text: The index goes stale the moment the next event is appended.  Freshness is now *answerable*; keeping it fresh is a scheduling decision this module does not make.
claims.why: No freshness tracking or scheduling code in this chunk.

observations.what: complete_prefix_end uses a while loop that may be infinite if file size is 0? Actually returns 0 early. For non-zero, loop reads chunks from end; if no newline found, position becomes 0 and loop ends. Edge case: file with only one line without newline: position becomes 0 and returns 0 correctly.

scan_journal starts line_number at 0 and increments before assigning to entry. For first line after start offset, line_number becomes 1. If start offset is not 0, line numbering is relative to file start, not to start offset. This may be intentional but could mislead.
journal_position handles missing file and shrunken file gracefully by returning position 0 with hash of empty string. This is safe but may mask races.
